title: The Harbor of Rosewater Lane
premise: Petra Coldharbour has spent a decade hiding behind the counter of Rosewater Lane's last bookshop, raising her daughter alone and refusing to touch the Coldharbour inheritance that ruined her family. When her estranged, power-hungry brother forces a family reunion to settle their late mother's will, Petra hires charming newcomer Elias Wren to pose as her date—only to find the pretense dissolving into something dangerously real. As the will's terms threaten to hand the harborfront, and the bookshop's fate, to her brother's development scheme, Petra must confront the mirror: the ways she inherited her mother's habit of disappearing. In the end, she claims both the inheritance and her own name, chooses Elias openly, and reopens the bookshop as something new.
about_author: Xanthe Hartwell is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who writes love stories set in small towns where everyone knows your business and nobody knows your heart. She lives near the water with an unruly garden and a shelf of romances she refuses to alphabetize.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A lawyer's letter arrives: the reading of Marguerite Coldharbour's will coincides with the family reunion at Harbor House, attendance mandatory to claim any inheritance. Petra's daughter Junie begs her to go; Petra wants to burn the letter. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by a flicker of longing for a family she pretends not to want.

chapters.title: A Stranger on Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias Wren, newly arrived restoring boats at the marina, wanders into the bookshop seeking a map of the harbor and leaves having bought three novels he doesn't need. He notices how Petra dims when a customer mentions the Coldharbour reunion. Emotional beat: curiosity kindling into fascination.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cornered by her brother Marcus's phone call—smug, certain she'll slink in alone—Petra impulsively asks Elias to be her fake date for the reunion weekend. He agrees with disarming ease, asking only one condition: no lies between them afterward. Emotional beat: reckless hope tangled with guilt over the deception.

chapters.title: Harbor House
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The reunion begins: marble halls, old grievances, Marcus performing magnanimity while courting investors for a marina development. Elias plays his role too well, charming even Petra's sharp-tongued aunt. Emotional beat: Petra watching Elias fit into her world and hating how much she wants it to be true.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Over dessert, the performance slips—Elias defends Petra against Marcus's veiled cruelty with unscripted ferocity, and under the table their hands find each other. Later, on the terrace, they almost kiss before Junie interrupts. Emotional beat: the fake date turning real, terrifyingly fast.

chapters.title: The Will of Marguerite Coldharbour
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The will is read: the harborfront estate goes to whoever 'truly carries the Coldharbour name'—a clause Marcus interprets as his by right of ambition, and which the lawyer reveals hinges on a letter Marguerite left sealed. Petra learns her mother once wrote to her, every year, letters never sent. Emotional beat: grief reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers Petra has been quietly selling off her own beloved first editions to keep the bookshop solvent—and confronts her about the walls she builds. Their fight exposes her deepest fear: that she is becoming her mother, loving people from a safe distance. Emotional beat: raw honesty breaking the romance open.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra finds her mother's unsent letters hidden in the bookshop's attic—confessions revealing Marguerite surrendered her own dreams to Marcus's father, and named Petra, not Marcus, as heir if she ever stopped hiding. Marcus, tipped off, arrives to seize them. Emotional beat: fury and inheritance colliding.

chapters.title: High Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Climax. At the harborfront hearing, Marcus produces forged documents claiming the estate; Elias publicly renounces his role as 'fake date,' declaring real love instead, risking everything. Petra stands, reads her mother's letter aloud, and claims the inheritance and her own voice. Emotional beat: courage at full flood.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Resolution. Months later: the bookshop reopens expanded onto the harborfront, Junie shelving books beside her, Marcus diminished but given a path to make amends. Elias's boat is moored outside; he moves in slowly, honestly. Petra forgives the woman in the mirror. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy—an open door at last.
